children.title: Cycle 15 · Synthesis of Intelligent Disobedience and Reasoning Blind Spots

detail.title: Synthesis of Intelligent Disobedience and Reasoning Blind Spots
detail.summary: This update revises findings on intelligent disobedience and LLM reasoning blind spots, synthesizing evidence on heuristic search and decision-theoretic agents. It formalizes intelligent disobedience as the ability to reject locally optimal heuristic search paths and identifies 'blind spots' in LLM reasoning as structural failures in search space exploration, consistent with heuristic search limitations.

children.title: Formalizing Intelligent Disobedience via Heuristic Search

detail.title: Formalizing Intelligent Disobedience via Heuristic Search
detail.summary: Intelligent disobedience in safety-critical systems can be modeled as a deviation from optimal heuristic search paths when an agent identifies that following the assigned objective violates a higher-level safety constraint. By framing disobedience as a search problem, agents can evaluate the search space dynamically rather than following pre-set heuristics.
detail.reason: Revising synthesis to incorporate new formal foundations for search and heuristic modeling.

children.title: Revision of LLM Reasoning Blind Spots and Epistemic Awareness

detail.title: Revision of LLM Reasoning Blind Spots and Epistemic Awareness
detail.summary: LLM 'blind spots' are increasingly identifiable as failures in heuristic search where the model fixates on local optima. This synthesis connects EACL 2026 reasoning findings with formal search limitations, suggesting that systematic improvement requires explicit navigation of the search space rather than implicit prediction.
detail.reason: Revising reasoning blind spot analysis to incorporate classical search literature.
